title: Derive the K*machine_epsilon noise floor (leg 367's E5 measurement) from standard nonsymmetric eigensolver backward-stability theory, or name exactly the step that resists.

preconditions.leg_367: landed at commit 728e0cc; classified leg 356's exact-pinning ground (iii) UNVERIFIED-ASSUMPTION, empirically corroborated; canonical_order()'s ordering scheme HOLDS on the weaker fact.
preconditions.leg_356: experiments/journal/leg_356.md; repaired experiments/p2_route_e_v1_spectrum.py's canonical_order(kept, dist, round_dp=6) -- re-sorts kept eigenvalues by (round(Re,6), -Im) to defeat a noise-driven sort on a near-degenerate key. item (10) is the accumulator marker owed to this record.

solver_identification.matrix: RescaledFlow.generator(b) = S^{-1} @ jacobian(b), a dense K x K REAL, GENERAL (non-symmetric, non-normal) matrix -- solver/rescaled_spectrum.py lines ~240-248
solver_identification.routine: numpy.linalg.eigvals -- its own docstring states 'implemented using _geev LAPACK routines' -- i.e. LAPACK dgeev for a real double-precision general matrix (verified by reading numpy 2.5.1's numpy/linalg/_linalg.py source directly in this environment).
solver_identification.algorithm: dgeev: Hessenberg reduction by orthogonal similarity followed by the (implicit double-shift) QR algorithm on the Hessenberg form -- the standard normwise-backward-stable algorithm for the general (non-Hermitian) dense eigenproblem (Golub & Van Loan, Matrix Computations, 4th ed., Ch.7 'Unsymmetric Eigenvalue Problems', esp. the Francis/QR-algorithm sections; Wilkinson, The Algebraic Eigenvalue Problem, Ch.5-6, is the original backward-stability source).
solver_identification.critical_fact: numpy.linalg.eigvals wraps dgeev, NOT dgeevx. dgeevx is the LAPACK driver that additionally computes and returns the reciprocal eigenvalue condition numbers RCONDE (denoted s_i below) that LAPACK's own error-bound theorems require as an input. The solver's actual call site never requests s_i, so no error bound of the kind this leg investigates is available in-band from the call the solver makes -- it can only be reconstructed offline, read-only, from the returned matrix.

literature_ground.primary_source: LAPACK Users' Guide (Anderson et al., 3rd ed.), Chapter 4, 'Further Details: Error Bounds for the Nonsymmetric Eigenproblem' (www.netlib.org/lapack/lug/node91.html - node93.html), fetched and quoted directly in this leg (not from memory).
literature_ground.backward_stability_statement: All algorithms for the nonsymmetric eigenproblem are normwise backward stable: they compute the exact eigenvalues, eigenvectors and invariant subspaces of a slightly perturbed matrix A+E, where ||E|| <= p(n) * eps * ||A||, p(n) a modestly-growing function of n (the LAPACK guide does not give p(n) a closed polynomial form; it is treated as an unspecified, empirically modest constant, the same posture LAPACK takes for its other backward-error bounds, e.g. the GLM/LSE routines' q(m,n,p)).
literature_ground.asymptotic_bound_table_4_5: For a SIMPLE eigenvalue: |lambda_hat_i - lambda_i| <~ ||E||_2 / s_i, where s_i is the reciprocal eigenvalue condition number (LAPACK's RCONDE, = |y_i^H x_i| for unit-norm right/left eigenvectors x_i, y_i -- i.e. 1/s_i is exactly the classical Wilkinson eigenvalue condition number kappa(lambda_i)). The guide states explicitly this bound holds only 'for sufficiently small ||E||, which is why it is called asymptotic.'
literature_ground.global_bound_table_4_6: A GUARANTEED bound (true for all E, not just asymptotically small E) exists for an eigenvalue CLUSTER (a simple eigenvalue is the size-1 case): |lambda_hat_I - lambda_I| <= 2*||E||_2 / s_I, but ONLY under the explicit stated precondition ||E||_F < s_i * sep_i / 4 (sep_i = the separation of the eigenvalue/cluster from the rest of the spectrum). If that precondition fails, Table 4.6's bound is not licensed to be applied at all.
literature_ground.always_true_disk_bound: Independently of the precondition above, LAPACK's guide also states a Gershgorin/Bauer-Fike-type disk theorem, true for every E with no smallness precondition: every computed eigenvalue lies in the union of n disks, the i-th disk centered at lambda_i with radius n*||E||_2/s_i.

measurement.method: Read-only import of solver.rescaled_spectrum (no repo file edited), scratch script outside the repo (per leg 367's precedent), computed at a=0 for K=48,96,144,192: (1) ||A||_2 via SVD, (2) the full eigendecomposition of A and of A^T with a global least-distance greedy assignment (not per-index argmin, to avoid mismatching under near-degenerate eigenvalues) to pair each right eigenvector x_i with its matching left eigenvector y_i, giving s_i = |y_i^H x_i| (unit-normalized) directly, (3) the nearest-neighbor spectral gap as a sep_i proxy, all for the SAME non-structural eigenvalue leg 367 tracked (max|Re(lambda)| over the K-1 non-structural eigenvalues, excluding the isolated -1 mode).
measurement.backward_error_estimate: ||E||_2 ~ p(K)*eps*||A||_2, computed at p(K)=10K (an upper-end, pessimistic-for-the-theory rule-of-thumb) as the headline case below. Robustness checked at the OTHER extreme too: p(K)=1 (||E||=eps*||A||, no K-growth at all -- the smallest value any reading of LAPACK's 'modestly growing' language permits) still gives ratio ||E||/threshold = 22 to 77 at the four K values (vs 1.8e4-7.4e4 at p(K)=10K) -- the Table-4.6 precondition fails at BOTH ends of the plausible p(K) range, so the conclusion does not depend on which constant is chosen.

disk_bound_evaluated.note: The always-true disk bound n*||E||_2/s_i, evaluated at the SAME (K, s_worst, E_norm_est) rows above
disk_bound_evaluated.compare: leg 356's canonical_order() threshold is 1e-6; leg 367's measured floor is 1.8e-14 to 3.2e-13. The disk bound (1.4e5 to 1.4e7) is 11-13 orders of magnitude ABOVE leg 356's 1e-6 threshold and 18.8-19.7 orders of magnitude ABOVE leg 367's measured floor -- true, unconditionally, but wholly uninformative at either scale.

resisting_step: Standard non-normal (general, non-symmetric) dense eigensolver backward-error theory does not derive leg 367's observed K*machine_epsilon noise floor. Two separate, independently sourced failures, both quoted from LAPACK's own error-bound theorems (not invented): (1) the ASYMPTOTIC bound |lambda_hat-lambda| <~ ||E||_2/s_i is explicitly licensed ONLY for 'sufficiently small ||E||' -- and Table 4.6's own precondition for the alternative GUARANTEED bound, ||E||_F < s_i*sep_i/4, is violated by 1.8e4 to 7.4e4 (four to five orders of magnitude) at every one of leg 367's four K values, using the measured eigenvalue condition numbers (kappa = 1/s_i ~ 6.2e14 to 9.5e14 for the specific ill-conditioned non-structural eigenvalues in question, computed directly from RescaledFlow.generator's own matrix, not assumed). (2) The one bound that IS always true regardless of that precondition -- LAPACK's Gershgorin/Bauer-Fike disk theorem, radius n*||E||_2/s_i -- is honestly evaluable without any smallness assumption, and evaluates to 1.4e2 (K=48) through 1.4e4 (K=192): eight to ten orders of magnitude ABOVE both leg 356's 1e-6 threshold and leg 367's measured floor. So the theory that is unconditionally licensed to apply here (the disk bound, evaluating to 1.4e5-1.4e7 across the four K values) is true but vacuous -- 11-13 orders of magnitude above leg 356's 1e-6 threshold and 18.8-19.7 orders of magnitude above leg 367's measured floor, far too loose to explain, or even be consistent in any informative sense with, the tightness of the observed floor -- and the theory that WOULD be tight enough (the asymptotic bound) is not licensed to apply, because this solver's own matrix is demonstrably too ill-conditioned (non-normal, near-degenerate discretized-continuum eigenvalues with individual condition numbers ~1e15) for the smallness precondition the bound requires. A further, structural fact compounds this: the call site the solver actually uses (numpy.linalg.eigvals -> LAPACK dgeev) never computes s_i (RCONDE) at all -- that requires dgeevx, which this module does not call -- so even the loose disk bound is not available in-band from the solver's own output; every number in the 'measurement' table above had to be reconstructed offline, read-only, outside the module under test.
consequence_for_leg_356_marker_item_10: The ground for canonical_order()'s round_dp=6 (1e-6) threshold stays EMPIRICAL, exactly as leg 367 left it (UNVERIFIED-ASSUMPTION, empirically corroborated) -- it is NOT upgraded to a derived floating-point ground by this leg. Standard backward-stability/perturbation theory for the general non-normal eigenproblem, honestly applied with the solver's own matrix and LAPACK's own quoted theorems, does not certify the observed K*eps shape: it is either not licensed to apply (asymptotic bound) or true-but-many-orders-of-magnitude-too-loose to be informative (disk bound). This does not threaten leg 356's repair -- the repair's correctness only needs the empirical floor to sit below 1e-6, which leg 367 already re-confirmed with ~6.5 orders of margin, and this leg changes nothing about that empirical fact. It only forecloses one specific route (generic non-normal backward-error theory) to upgrading that empirical fact to a theorem; the gap is named, not papered over.
what_would_close_the_gap: A structural, operator-specific argument (not generic dense-matrix perturbation theory) -- e.g. a proof that the specific quantity Re(lambda) (as opposed to lambda itself) is well-conditioned under the real, structured perturbations dgeev's rounding actually produces on THIS matrix, or a cluster/invariant-subspace argument exploiting the fact that the ill-conditioned eigenvalues form a discretized continuum rather than isolated near-degeneracies. Neither was attempted here (out of territory: no solver/ edits, no new derivation of that scope) and neither is claimed to exist.
reproduction: Read-only import of solver.rescaled_spectrum.continuation/RescaledFlow.generator at a=0, K in {48,96,144,192}; np.linalg.eig(A) and np.linalg.eig(A.T) with a global greedy nearest-distance assignment (not per-index argmin) to pair right/left eigenvectors; s_i = |y_i^H x_i| for unit-normalized vectors. Full script kept outside the repo per leg 367's precedent (territory bars new solver/experiments modules).
